desc:
The array digits holds the decimal digits of a number, most significant digit first. You may swap two of the digits (any two positions) at most once. Return the digit array of the largest number you can obtain. Leading zeros are not an issue: all arrays have the same length, so comparing numbers is the same as comparing arrays element by element from the left.

digits = [2, 7, 3, 6]
result = [7, 2, 3, 6]

digits = [9, 9, 7, 3]
result = [9, 9, 7, 3]
hints: Trying all pairs of positions is O(n<sup>2</sup>) pairs. Think about which position should receive a bigger digit.
The leftmost position that has a larger digit somewhere to its right is the one to fix. Which digit should come in?

Record the last index of each digit 0..9. For each position from the left, look for the largest digit greater than the current one whose last index lies to the right; swap with that last index. Taking the last occurrence puts the small digit as far right as possible.
editorial: To maximise the array lexicographically, improve the leftmost position that can be improved. That is the first index i that has a strictly larger digit somewhere to its right. At that position put the largest such digit.

If that largest digit occurs several times, take its last occurrence: the smaller digit that gets moved out lands as far right as possible, where it hurts least. Precomputing last[d] for the ten digits and checking digits 9 down to digits[i] + 1 at each position gives O(10 n) = O(n) time and O(1) space.
If no position has a larger digit to its right, the digits are already non-increasing and the number cannot be improved; return it unchanged.
